name: Habshan Gas Processing Complex
description: ADNOC Gas's main onshore hub: five plants with 14 processing trains and 6.1 bscfd capacity, plus an onsite sulphur granulation plant.

name: Habshan 5 Gas Processing Plant
description: The newest of the Habshan plants, built under the Integrated Gas Development (IGD) scheme to process offshore gas piped from Das Island; ADNOC's 2017 inauguration release gave a feed gas capacity of 2.32 bscfd, and ADNOC Gas says it houses some of the world's largest sulphur recovery units.

name: Bab Gas Processing Plant
description: One of ADNOC Gas's onshore associated-gas processing facilities, started up in 1981 alongside Asab and Buhasa; no site-level capacity is published on the ADNOC Gas operations page.

name: Asab Gas Processing Plant
description: Onshore associated-gas processing facility at the Asab field, started up in 1981 with a second plant (Asab 2) added in 2001; no site-level capacity is published on the ADNOC Gas operations page.

name: Buhasa Gas Processing Plant
description: Onshore associated-gas processing facility at the Bu Hasa field, started up in 1981; no site-level capacity is published on the ADNOC Gas operations page.

name: Ruwais NGL Fractionation Plant
description: The UAE's only NGL fractionation plant, with four fractionation trains at the Al Ruwais Industrial Complex producing ethane, LPG and paraffinic naphtha; a fifth train is being added under the Rich Gas Development programme.

name: Das Island LNG Plant
description: The UAE's only operating LNG export facility, with three LNG trains of about 6 mtpa plus five gas processing trains.

name: Taweelah Gas Compression Plant
description: Sales-gas compression station about 50 km north of Abu Dhabi city, inaugurated in November 2018, with three 225 mmscfd trains (two running, one standby) for 450 mmscfd, fed by the Maqta-Taweelah pipeline to supply Abu Dhabi industry and the Northern Emirates.

name: Ruwais Sulphur Handling Terminal
description: Export terminal at the Al Ruwais Industrial Complex where granulated sulphur from Habshan is combined with sulphur from other ADNOC Gas and ADNOC Group operations and shipped; no terminal capacity is published.

name: Ruwais LNG Project
description: Two-train, 9.6 mtpa LNG export plant in Ruwais designed to run on clean grid power; FID was taken in 2024 and commissioning is expected in 2028.

name: MERAM Ethane Recovery Project
description: US$3.6 billion project located mainly at the Habshan 5 plant, with a 120 km NGL pipeline to Ruwais, to deliver about 3.4 mtpa of ethane and NGLs for Borouge 4 and export; first gas was reported introduced in November 2026.

name: Bab Gas Cap Project
description: Planned gas processing development expected to add over 1.8 bscfd of processing capacity; at FEED stage and pre-FID according to ADNOC Gas's 2025 integrated report.

name: Jebel Dhanna Terminal
description: Onshore crude export terminal built in the 1960s that has operated as the Murban export facility; one of two export terminals operated by ADNOC Onshore.

name: Fujairah Main Oil Terminal
description: Gulf of Oman export terminal at the end of the approximately 406 km Habshan-Fujairah crude pipeline (ADCOP), with a reported capacity of 1.5-1.8 million bpd; a second West-East pipeline from Jebel Dhanna is planned for 2027.

name: Zirku Island Terminal
description: Offshore island where crude from Upper Zakum, Umm Al Dalkh and Satah is processed, stored and exported; the terminal has two single-point-mooring berths.

name: Das Island Oil Terminal
description: Offshore island terminal that processes, stores and exports crude from the Zakum, Umm Shaif, Bunduq and Abu Al Bukhoosh fields.

name: ADNOC L&S Mussafah Integrated Logistics Base
description: ADNOC L&S's main offshore supply and logistics base, described by MEED as the largest integrated logistics base in the Gulf region; the company also has bases in Ruwais and Fujairah.

name: Bab Field
description: One of ADNOC Onshore's four asset groups and one of its largest oil fields, also the site of the Habshan gas complex; trade press has reported capacity of around 450,000 bpd (dated figure).

name: Bu Hasa Field
description: ADNOC Onshore's largest oil field and a standalone asset group; trade press has reported capacity of about 650,000 bpd (dated figure).

name: Asab Field
description: Oil field in ADNOC Onshore's South East asset group.

name: Sahil Field
description: Oil field in ADNOC Onshore's South East asset group, alongside Asab, Shah, Qusahwira and Mender.

name: Qusahwira Field
description: Oil field in the far south of Abu Dhabi, part of ADNOC Onshore's South East asset group together with the Shah and Mender fields.

name: Al Dabb'iya Field
description: Coastal oil field in ADNOC Onshore's North East Bab (NEB) asset group, which also includes Rumaitha and Shanayel.

name: Rumaitha Field
description: Oil field in ADNOC Onshore's North East Bab (NEB) asset group and an injection site for CO2 captured by the Al Reyadah CCUS facility.

name: Shah Gas Plant
description: Ultra-sour gas field and processing plant in the far south of Abu Dhabi, expanded to 1.45 bscfd in 2023 and a major sulphur producer.

name: Upper Zakum Field
description: Giant offshore oil field developed from four artificial islands, with crude piped to Zirku Island; production capacity was reported at 1 million bpd in July 2025 with a 1.2 million bpd target for 2027.

name: Lower Zakum Field
description: Offshore oil field whose crude is processed and exported at Das Island; reported capacity of around 425,000 bpd with a planned expansion to 450,000 bpd.

name: Umm Shaif Field
description: Offshore oil and gas field whose crude goes to Das Island and whose gas feeds the Das Island and Habshan plants; reported oil capacity of about 275,000 bpd.

name: Nasr Field
description: Offshore oil field about 130 km northwest of Abu Dhabi whose full-field development raised capacity from 22,000 to 65,000 bpd in 2019.

name: Umm Lulu Field
description: Offshore oil field developed together with SARB in the SARB and Umm Lulu concession (ADNOC 60%).

name: Satah Al Razboot (SARB) Field
description: Offshore oil field in the SARB and Umm Lulu concession, with a planned 100,000 bpd from the two fields combined; ADNOC took FID on a separate SARB Deep Gas development tied back to Das Island in January 2026.

name: Hail and Ghasha Development
description: Offshore ultra-sour gas development in the Ghasha Concession targeting 1.8 bscfd of gas by 2030, with capture of 1.5 million tonnes a year of CO2; FID has been taken and fabrication is under way.

name: Belbazem Offshore Block
description: Offshore block about 120 km northwest of Abu Dhabi city with three fields (Belbazem, Umm Al Salsal, Umm Al Dholou); first production was announced in March 2024, with planned peak output of 45,000 bpd of oil and 27 mmscfd of gas.

name: Ruwais Refinery (East and West)
description: The UAE's largest refining complex, comprising Ruwais East (about 400,000-420,000 bpd) and Ruwais West (417,000 bpd), with a Crude Flexibility Project designed to allow up to 420,000 bpd of heavier, sourer crude.

name: Borouge Ruwais Complex (Borouge 1-3)
description: Integrated polyolefins complex in Ruwais with 4.5 mtpa capacity before Borouge 4, receiving about 14,000 tonnes a day of ethane from ADNOC Gas.

name: Borouge 4
description: US$6.2 billion expansion with a 1.5 mtpa ethane cracker and 1.4 mtpa of polyolefins capacity; polymer production was reported to have started in early April 2026 with ramp-up continuing as remaining units are commissioned.

name: Fertil Ruwais Fertilizer Complex
description: Two-train integrated ammonia and granular urea complex in Ruwais that ADNOC contributed to Fertiglobe in 2019; the Fertil-2 train is rated at 2,000 tonnes a day of ammonia and 3,500 tonnes a day of urea.

name: TA'ZIZ Industrial Chemicals Zone
description: Chemicals zone in Ruwais whose first phase targets 4.7 mtpa of products by the end of 2028, including a 1 mtpa low-carbon ammonia plant (with Fertiglobe, Mitsui and GS Energy; EPC over 90% complete in November 2026) and a 1.8 mtpa methanol plant with Proman targeted for 2028.

name: ADNOC Industrial Gases Ruwais Air Separation Plant
description: Air separation plant in the Ruwais industrial zone supplying nitrogen and oxygen, operated by the ADNOC-Linde joint venture set up in 2007 as Elixier.

name: Al Reyadah CCUS Facility
description: Carbon capture facility adjacent to Emirates Steel in Mussafah, commissioned in 2016, capturing up to 800,000 tonnes a year of CO2 that is piped about 43 km for enhanced oil recovery at the Rumaitha and Bab fields.
